page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: From sucrose
lines: Sucrose is boiled with dilute acid in
Glucose is less soluble in alcohol and
steps.why: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives glucose and fructose together, so the method is only useful if the two can be separated. Alcohol does that: glucose is the less soluble of the two and comes out of solution while fructose stays dissolved.
common_mistakes: Writing that sucrose gives glucose only. It gives glucose and fructose in equal amounts.
Leaving out the acid. Sucrose does not hydrolyse in plain boiling water at any useful rate.
steps.memory_tip: Sucrose plus acid gives both hexoses; glucose is the less soluble and comes out first.
steps.margin_note: The equation is the fastest way to earn this mark. Name the acid and both products.

steps.label: From starch

lines.text: Large scale: starch with dilute H₂SO₄

lines: Conditions: dilute H₂SO₄, 393 K, and a
Starch is cheap, so this is the route used
for glucose on a large scale.
steps.why: Starch is a polymer of glucose alone, so its hydrolysis gives one product and needs no separation, which is exactly what a large scale process requires. The raised temperature and pressure bring the hydrolysis of a long polymer to completion in a workable time.
common_mistakes: Writing concentrated H₂SO₄. The acid is dilute; concentrated sulphuric acid would char the starch.
Leaving out the conditions. 393 K and 2 to 3 atm are printed in the answer key and are expected.
steps.memory_tip: Starch is glucose only, so the industrial route uses starch, not sucrose.
steps.margin_note: Write the equation with the conditions over the arrow. The three numbers are what mark this step.

insider_note: Two methods, and the second one carries the numbers: dilute H₂SO₄, 393 K, 2 to 3 atm. Write both equations; they are quicker than sentences and they mark themselves.
